reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, setup, CLI readiness and domain terms. Ask accepts deliberate Projectless questions without enabling the cwd Project. Send and ask, including held waits and OpenCode, still refuse a Project the User disabled: omitting request identity never overrides that decision. The skill and OpenCode reference state this boundary; outside a Project, Projectless requests still work without Enablement state. Grok denies unregistered question cards before opening and uses the same recommended-suffix normalization as the Claude picker to preserve exact registered questions and the questions-off, disabled-Project and signed-out cases. OpenCode 1 carries free text and up to ten questions, while the protocol still permits only one recommended choice per question; its reference states that limit and the 110-second held fallback for workers, Projectless waits and missing hand-backs. Activation remedies preserve the original question, wait mode and flags and give an honest conversation fallback. Empty close is a successful no-op; replies and legacy send waits retain their shipped exit-3 contract, documented per command. Foreground replies are quoted with the existing transport limit and printed before acknowledgement instructions; ordered text parts are not automatically declared superseded. The Codex card JSON describes terminal settlement and closing a dropped-card conversation answer. CLI pointers use the supported guidance command, retired flags remain hidden and accepted, retry refusals explain recovery, provider rejection names its failure on stderr, and credential-store remedies carry the plaintext/shared-machine caveat. Setup and readiness need no further behavioral change; ownership, activation context and answer-injection wording remain as on main. Refusal JSON has an additive reason distinguishing answer_cannot_return from routing_not_ready while preserving released error codes. The result reference documents the existing pending-reply shapes, JSON error limits and text-only receive command.
